correctness.rationale: For a distinct-letter permutation order R, greedy scattered embedding in R^k is equivalent to at most k−1 weak descents of the word; an insertion cannot lower a descent count. An inclusion-maximal common subsequence saturates descent budgets for both orders P=AxyB and Q=AyxB, since otherwise a feasible additional letter can be inserted. The two almost-identical linear orders determine a no-free-insertion transition graph: permissible maximal words concatenate r forced A, B blocks separated by nonempty alternating x/y segments. Each reset consumes one descent in each order and internal xy and yx transitions consume the remaining exactly k−r each. Then lengths are 2k+(q−3)r, r=1..k, and the coefficient enumerator comes from H=(2+u+v)/(1−uv) for alternating segments. Diagonal extraction of (2+u+v)/(1−uv(3+u+v)) yields central binomial binom(2k,k). Independent exhaustive distinct-subsequence intersection and single-insertion maximality for q=4, P=0123, Q=0213, k=1..3 found total MCS 2,6,20 with length histograms {3:2}, {5:2,6:4}, {7:2,8:10,9:8}. These do not establish arbitrary k; the symbolic proof does.
residual_risks: The hypotheses q>=4 and adjacent swap are essential; the q=3 case has no shorter maximal words and needs separate treatment.
Word counts distinguish distinct spellings not embeddings; no extrapolation from k<=3 is claimed.
